Extended Palette · Technical Theming

Extended Palette

The canonical extended color palette for technical theming — full light/dark modes and IDE color themes. It extends the base personal palette while keeping the three brand cores (green, gold, blue) as the identity: warm and earthy with high pop and contrast, plus two well-separated support hues (terracotta & plum) placed in open zones of the color wheel so the language stays clean across syntax and UI surfaces.

Brand cores

Unchanged from the base palette — the identity anchors. Per-mode accents below are saturated/brightened versions of these tuned for contrast in context.

Surfaces, neutrals & accents

Light gets a crisp warm-white canvas with deepened, saturated accents. Dark uses a warm desaturated background (lifted off near-black, Monokai-style) so the vivid accents pop. The cores plus two well-separated supports (terracotta, plum) carry the palette; soft tints are for subtle backgrounds (selection, hover, callouts).

Hue spacing

Each hue occupies its own zone of the color wheel rather than crowding the warm quarter, which keeps the language clean — no hue reads as a muddied version of its neighbor. The two supports (terracotta, plum) sit in open zones, and the error red is set apart from terracotta:

16° terracotta #F97C3E (support) 42° gold #F7B61F 149° green #45CB85 205° blue #54ACEC 290° plum #C488D6 (support) 355° red #E54552 (errors)

Semantic / status

Status colors reuse the cores where they read naturally (success = green, info = blue, warning = gold) and add one earthy brick red for errors, since none of the cores reads as danger.

Syntax highlighting (IDE)

Cores carry the identity tokens — green keywords (the signature, most frequent, like Monokai's pink slot), blue functions, and gold numbers/constants (short, sparse → gold's loud yellow only gleams occasionally). The two well-separated supports do the rest: plum for strings and terracotta for types. Dark accents run bright for Monokai-style pop; light accents are deepened for contrast on the warm-white canvas.

// fetch a user profile import { User } from "./types"; const API = "https://api.example.com"; const MAX_RETRIES = 3; async function getUser(id: number): Promise<User> { const res = await fetch(`${API}/users/${id}`); if (!res.ok) throw new Error("not found"); return res.json(); }

Light mode

string (plum) #834A86 / #C488D6
type / class (terracotta) #B0451C / #F97C3E
error / invalid #A0202E / #E54552
comment (italic) #756E58 / #897F66
punctuation / operator #4A4336 / #B2A98E
variable / text #221E14 / #F6F1E3
